items.q: Why is evaluating enterprise agents hard?
items.a: There's **no public benchmark** and **domain experts are too busy** to grade.

items.q: What limited the 2024 telecom RAG team?
items.a: Weekly expert panels allowed only **one trial a week**, and experts **often disagreed**.

items.q: What's Weill's core rule for agents?
items.a: **If you cannot grade the agent, you can't make it better.**

items.q: How do you generate RAG tests without experts?
items.a: Start from a **page**, have an LLM **write a question**, then check with code if retrieval finds it.

items.q: What changed once they had an automatic test set?
items.a: From **one eval a week to dozens a day**, and accuracy rose by **removing complexity**.

items.q: What's the strongest contract benchmark they built?
items.a: **Remove a clause** from a signed contract and see if the agent **notices it's missing**.
Change something **irrelevant** (supplier name, clause order, rerun) and check the **output doesn't change**.

items.q: How do templates multiply test cases?
items.a: Fill the blanks with **arrays of values**, some **breaking rules**, so you know the right flags.

items.q: Why avoid LLM-as-judge when you can?
items.a: It adds **noise** nearly **as hard to fix as the task**; prefer **exact match or code**.

items.q: What should expert feedback be used for?
items.a: To **generate better tests**, not to patch the agent directly.
